text:
ajit: Hi team, Ajit here (new runtime dev). Trying to build the runtime from source on my M1 MacBook Pro. Hitting errors because macOS can't have CUDA installed. Anyone have the recommended dev flow for people on ARM laptops? :wave:
linh: welcome Ajit! we usually do local dev for CPU-only stuff, and use the remote build fleet for GPU builds. For full integration (nvcc / CUDA) you'll need to ssh into a linux gpu build host.
omar: +1. don't try to install CUDA on mac. Use the build host or a devcontainer that cross-builds.
ajit: thanks — any docs on ssh host names / creds? I tried ssh build@buildbox but got permission denied.
paige: pinging infra — @devops-bot can you confirm build host access for new hires?
devops-bot: Hi! New hire access flow: request a ticket in #help with your SSO username. Once approved, you'll get a short-lived SSH cert. See /handbook/dev-onboarding -> "GPU build hosts".
ajit: got it. while i wait, is there a way to run unit tests locally without CUDA? Some tests hit nvcc at configure time.
linh: yes, run the cmake flag to disable CUDA: `cmake -DENABLE_CUDA=OFF -S . -B build/local` then `cmake --build build/local -j8`. That lets you iterate on CPU code and unit tests.
ajit: when I tried that I still got a configure error: `Could NOT find CUDA: Found unsuitable version "" from NOTFOUND`
omar: ah that happens if the configure script blindly probes nvcc. Try `export SKIP_CUDA_PROBE=1` before running cmake, we put that guard in the top-level CMakeLists.
ajit: cool, `export SKIP_CUDA_PROBE=1` fixed configure. Build fails later with a linker error referencing `libdevice` when I run the integration target on the remote host. Example:```ld: cannot find -lcudadevrt```
paige: that one usually means the nvcc toolchain path isn't on LD_LIBRARY_PATH or CUDA_HOME isn't set for the build job. On our build hosts we use the module system. Try `module load cuda/12.1` before building on the host.
ajit: on the remote host `module load cuda/12.1` worked but I'm still seeing `ptxas: error: Unsupported gpu architecture 'compute_70'` — the build is using compute_70 but the host has A100 (compute_80).
omar: we have a tool that picks PTX archs based on TARGET_ARCH env. If you're using the autoset, override with `export TARGET_ARCH=sm_80`. Also check `tools/select-kernels.sh` in the repo.
ajit: setting `TARGET_ARCH=sm_80` made that error go away. Thanks.
sam: FYI Ajit, for faster iteration we have a lightweight docker image (cpu-only) and a short-lived GPU dev image on the fleet (`redwood/dev-gpu:latest`) — you can `docker run --rm -it redwood/dev-gpu:latest /bin/bash` after you have SSH access. It mounts your repo and runs the same build script.
ajit: perfect — I'll raise the access ticket now. One last quick Q: is there a recommended checklist for first-week runtime tasks (build, run unit tests, smoke on GPU, basic perf run)?
linh: yes — there's a checklist in the onboarding doc: 1) clone repo + submodules, 2) run `./scripts/bootstrap --dev`, 3) build CPU w/ `SKIP_CUDA_PROBE=1`, 4) request GPU host access, 5) run `./scripts/build --target=gpu` on the host, 6) run one smoke perf harness `tools/perf/run_smoke.sh`.
ajit: thanks everyone, super helpful. I'll update thread with ticket number once infra approves. :thumbsup:
